title: Christopher Whalen: I'm Selling Bank Stocks & Buying Metals and Energy
speaker: Christopher Whalen

macro_themes.view: Long rates have risen on their own on inflation fears, policy noise and heavy AI-related debt issuance; ~7.5% mortgages are the new normal.
Fiscal pressure will force the Fed to buy bonds again aggressively, which is bullish for gold.
Energy, diesel and fertilizer shocks keep inflation well above 2% for the next couple of years absent a deflationary shock.
Bottom of the K-shaped economy is weak; consumer lender delinquencies and credit costs will rise, consumer finance volumes fall in Q4.
Shift to a buyer's market with a 5-10% decline in median home prices over 12-18 months, not a crash.
Circular financing and overbuilt capex mean an AI correction is coming; some AI companies may not survive.
House likely goes Democratic with investigations; affordability will drive politics.

calls.reason: Fiscal situation will force the Fed back to QE; gold is an asymmetric medium-to-long-term trade and he has been adding on dips.
calls.quote: the fiscal situation in the United States, which is going to force the Fed to print money ... is going to be good for gold

calls.reason: Silver, like gold, is in short supply globally and a trade to put on and keep on; he has been adding as prices fell.
calls.quote: As the prices have come down with higher interest rates, I've been adding to both my gold and silver.

calls.reason: Best-managed mortgage REIT, ~14% yield on government-insured MBS; now trading near book after selling off, he will likely buy more.
calls.quote: My basis in Annaly is a little bit below book total um and I'll probably go buy more

calls.reason: Persian Gulf damage and refining shortages will drive energy majors higher; Chevron is the best-managed global oil company; hold, don't trade, and likely add over time.
calls.quote: the damage that's been done in the Persian Gulf, is going to drive them higher ... these are medium-term plays

calls.reason: Owns Exxon as part of his energy position; expects energy majors to move higher on Gulf supply damage.
calls.quote: You don't want to trade these. You want to hold them.

calls.reason: Long-held pipeline position; energy infrastructure benefits from the supply disruption.
calls.quote: I own Williams, which is a big pipeline company. I've owned that stock for years.

calls.reason: Sold Schwab at a profit in his quarterly rebalance as part of exiting all bank names ahead of higher rates and rising consumer delinquencies.
calls.quote: We got out of all of our bank names. We sold our position in Schwab which we had made some good money on.

calls.reason: Poorly managed versus JPMorgan, unrestructured securities book, AML fine; he has exited bank stocks generally.
calls.quote: BA needs to change ... they perform probably half as well as JP Morgan
